Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the RFI packet — we reviewed the section on runtime fallbacks and routing policies. Our technical team would like a more concrete playbook around the integration gateway handshake you reference (specifically: sequence of steps for traffic cutover, how traceability is preserved across model variants, and the minimum telemetry requirements you expect from our side during a canary).

Two asks: 1) can you share a short checklist mapping Redwood’s expected integration handshakes to our network/ACL requirements, and 2) a template mutual-action timeline that includes milestones you require to verify canary health (metrics, thresholds, escalation points).

We are targeting a phased activation in Q1; need these inputs to finalize our procurement timelines.

Thanks,

Hi Lily —

Appreciate the detailed read-through. I’m attaching a short questionnaire and our standard Mutual Action Plan template that we use to align sequence-of-steps for cutover and post-cutover verification. High-level answers below; Ben and Karthik will fill in the technical knobs.

Quick answers:
- Minimum telemetry: per-request trace id + latency and error counts at 1s granularity during canary; sampling for full token-level traces is fine at 1 in 50.
- Sequencing: (1) Shadowing for 48 hours with 100% production traffic replicated; (2) Canary at 1% for 4 hours with acceptance gates; (3) Gradual ramp 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 1-hour stabilization windows and rollback thresholds.
- Traceability: we propagate your trace-id in x-request-id and enrich with model_variant + server_id so both sides can join traces.

Attachments: Redwood_RFI_Integration_Questionnaire_v1.pdf, MutualActionPlan_EQ-1147.xlsx.

Ben/Karthik — can you confirm network requirements (ports, protocols), expected idle-timeouts for long-running chat sessions, and any recommended KV cache warm-up steps for Equitas’ usage patterns?

Marissa
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_RFI_Integration_Questionnaire_v1.pdf]

Subject: Re: RFI: Integration Gateway Handshake — sequencing & traceability

Lily / team —

Inline answers to the key technical points from the questionnaire:

> network / ACL requirements
- Outbound TLS 1.3 to Redwood endpoints on port 443.
- If using Private deployment: allow bi-directional VPN (IPsec) between Equitas ingress gateway and Redwood private endpoints (we'll provide IP ranges).
- Websocket keepalive: we recommend 30s ping for chat sessions; set idle timeout >= 5 minutes for long-lived sessions.

> canary telemetry and thresholds
- Success gate: error rate < 0.5% (5xx + model-failure signals) sustained for two consecutive 1-hour windows.
- Latency gate: p95 within 1.5x of baseline.
- Quality gate: sample 200 prompt completions and run automated evals (ROUGE/BLEU where applicable) or customer-defined prompt set — report regression <= 2%.

> KV cache warm-up
- Warm-up approach: run a warm-up job to prime top-1000 recognized prefixes (we can provide a tooling script). Expect warm-up traffic for ~30 minutes to reach 80% hit-rate depending on model and sequence lengths.

Attachments: MutualActionPlan_EQ-1147.xlsx, Network_Diagrams_EQ.zip (network ranges and VPN topology).

Happy to jump on a quick technical sync next week to walk through the diagram.

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Network_Diagrams_EQ.zip]

- For the canary ramp, we want an explicit backstop step where we hold at 5% for up to 8 hours before proceeding to 25% to allow manual QA sign-off.
